name: DUNE near detector — dark-sector program
full_name: Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment near-detector dark-sector program
summary: DUNE near detector — dark-sector program is proposed for the LBNF near-detector facility at Fermilab, Batavia, Illinois. It is cataloged as a distinct near-site beam dark-sector program, which should link to its parent DUNE experiment and remain distinct from far-detector Galactic-dark-matter searches.
detection_principle: A high-intensity proton beam produces dark-matter candidates, with near detectors recording electron/nucleon scattering or visible decays. DUNE-PRISM off-axis movement changes beam composition to help distinguish backgrounds.

results.summary: Sensitivity studies show off-axis data can improve several light-dark-matter and heavy-neutral-lepton scenarios; these are projections.

science_scope: Tests dark-sector models by producing candidate particles or portal mediators at accelerators. Invisible accelerator final states or mediator particles alone do not establish cosmic-dark-matter identity; lifetimes, abundance and other experiments must also be considered.
